sources.entry: Termix - Clientless web-based server management platform with SSH terminal, tunneling, and file editing capabilities. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Termix is a self-hosted, plugin-based server management platform with a web, desktop and mobile interface for SSH terminals, file management, Docker, remote desktop and more.
summary.what_it_does: The core handles saved hosts in nested folders with tags, reusable credentials, user and role sharing at connect/view/edit/manage levels, local accounts with sessions and API keys, and per-user encryption of secrets. Everything else is an optional plugin that can be turned on, off, or removed, including the SSH terminal, SFTP file manager, Docker/Podman and Kubernetes management, host metrics, tunnels, and remote desktop (RDP, VNC, Telnet). Plugins are installed from a Plugins tab and a community registry. Authentication add-ons include LDAP, SSO via OpenID Connect, passkeys, TOTP, and Vault/Step CA/OPKSSH-based short-lived SSH certificates. The README also lists session recording, session sharing, a Samba share manager, Proxmox and cloud host import, and a reverse proxy plugin. Databases can be SQLite (default), PostgreSQL, or MySQL. A Docker Compose sample is provided that runs a single container on port 8080.
use_cases: self-hosted SSH terminal and web-based server management
browse and edit remote files over SFTP
manage Docker containers on remote hosts
central access to homelab servers with shared credentials
browser-based RDP, VNC or Telnet sessions
record and share terminal sessions with a team
how_to_run: Save the sample docker-compose.yaml from the README (service image ghcr.io/termix-ssh/termix:latest, port 8080, volume termix-data mounted at /app/data).
Open http://localhost:8080 in a browser and create an account.
Alternatively, install the desktop or mobile app from the platform distribution list (see docs for per-platform steps).
notable: Plugin architecture: almost every feature (terminal, file manager, Docker, remote desktop) is a separate, removable plugin with its own repo
Runs as a web app, PWA, and native desktop and mobile apps for Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS, and Android
Built-in RDP, VNC and Telnet support without needing a separate gateway container
Hosts config plugin can keep hosts and sharing in a YAML or JSON file that reloads on change
Self-described as a free, self-hosted alternative to Termius
caveats: The README says Termix has no paid plans but relies on donations; a paid sponsor spot is offered by email
Many features (for example Docker, file manager, SSH terminal, remote desktop) live in separate plugin repos, so bug reports must go to the right repo
Cloud hosting is suggested for reliability, and a sponsor VPS provider is promoted in the README
keywords: share ssh hosts with my team
connect to my home servers remotely
